metadata.description: Menendez Market's Claude Code plugin marketplace

plugins.name: dev-orchestrator
plugins.description: Human-in-the-loop orchestrator for multi-step dev tasks with a two-level agent hierarchy. Recognized automatically: a UserPromptSubmit hook routes any prompt that asks for a plan or multi-step dev work, and every prompt in plan mode, to this skill first, without having to invoke it. Adopts the Lead's plan, or, when none is given, has a read-only Planner Agent on Opus (orch-planner, the plan-mode half of opusplan) draft one for the Lead to approve. Maps step dependencies and asks whether to run as a single session or multi-agent. In multi-agent mode each step gets a Task Agent on the latest Sonnet, in its own terminal (orch-sN-name) or inline for small steps and in its own git worktree (each finished step is applied to the Lead's tree as a checked, uncommitted patch), and starts as soon as its dependencies finish. Task Agents reuse the orchestrator's research and may spawn read-only Research Sub-agents (Sonnet 5) that use graphify first. Never runs tests: checks run once at the end. Never guesses on ambiguity, architecture, or destructive/git actions: escalates to the Lead. Trigger phrases: "create a plan", "crea un plan", "planifica", "orchestrate this", "use dev-orchestrator", "plan and delegate this task", "run this plan with task agents".

plugins.name: qa
plugins.description: QA agent suite: qa-orchestrator runs QA sessions (spawns test agents in parallel, collects results, triages bugs, generates reports); qa-happy-path tests the main UI flows with Playwright; qa-api-adversary tries to break the API (auth, input validation, duplicates, race conditions, malformed requests); qa-debugger applies minimal fixes for reported bugs; qa-personality-builder creates project-specific QA personalities. Installed together so the orchestrator always has the agents it spawns. Trigger with /qa-orchestrator, "run QA", "start QA session" or "test the PR".

plugins.name: unit-test-generator
plugins.description: Generate strict, isolated unit tests that follow the repo's own runner, mocking library and factories. Test data comes from Faker or existing factories (never hand-written objects), collaborators are mocked with the repo's mocking framework, data and time are seeded and deterministic, and every suite covers happy paths, branches, invalid input, boundaries, errors and side effects with the AAA pattern, and requires at least 90% line, statement, branch and function coverage on the unit under test. Never changes production code; reports suspected bugs instead. Trigger on "write unit tests for", "generate tests", "add test coverage", "refactor these tests", or /unit-test-generator.

plugins.name: api-handoff
plugins.description: Write and implement API handoff documents (Markdown) between frontend and backend. Backend → Frontend: documents the endpoint the frontend must consume. Frontend → Backend: specifies the endpoint the backend must build. Every endpoint gets its purpose, method and full path, auth, params, headers, the exact request body (field table + JSON example that must match), every success and error response, side effects and testable acceptance criteria, all extracted from real code (never invented; unknowns become TBD + open questions). Uses a fixed template with YAML front matter and ships a validator script, so any other Claude session can implement the handoff exactly and report contract mismatches. Trigger on "handoff", "write a handoff for the frontend", "handoff to backend", "implement this handoff", or /api-handoff.

plugins.name: clawd-pet
plugins.description: Clawd, the Claude pet from the desktop app, sits right above the Claude Code CLI prompt, on the right, with its laptop: it waves when you are around, turns sideways, pulls its laptop out and types with sparks flying while Claude works, wears a hard hat in plan mode, gets knocked out when a command fails, and falls asleep with a floating "Zzz" when you stop typing (60 s by default, set idleSeconds in /config). Type anything to wake it; /pet hides or shows it, and /pet color (or /config) changes its color: a palette name or any hex.
